RMD.thesis_one_line: Sleep-apnea device leader with a recurring-supplies business; GLP-1 fear hasn't hit volumes, and the stock is priced for less growth than it likely delivers - downgraded from full weight after a fact-check found the dossier's cited FY2027 guidance does not exist and missed a material MatrixCare divestiture.
kill_criteria: Quarterly organic revenue growth < 5% YoY for two consecutive quarters (vs the ~9-11% run-rate of the last five quarters).
Any second FDA recall/correction notice on a ResMed device within 12 months of the Astral action (June 2026).
GAAP or non-GAAP gross margin falls below 56% for two consecutive quarters.
Net debt/EBITDA turns positive and exceeds 1.0x (currently net cash).

RMD's first actual FY2027 quarterly guidance/commentary (expected with the Q1 FY2027 print, ~29 Oct 2026) shows organic revenue growth guided below 6%/year, or the >$1.85B FY2027 capital-return target is walked back.
Any delay, restatement or qualified review in the first PwC-reviewed 10-Q (Q1 FY2027); KPMG was dismissed and PwC appointed on 13 Aug 2026 (8-K Item 4.01)
key_adverse_facts: FDA Class I recall (most serious classification) on Astral 100/150 ventilators, ~168,069 devices globally, initiated 25 Jun 2026, FDA record Z-2735-2026, due to a supercapacitor component that can leak and cause loss of therapy delivery.

[Corrected 27 Sep 2026: removed - the '$75M revenue / $0.15 EPS' Astral headwind figure does not appear anywhere in the cited 8-K; it was fabricated along with the FY2027 guidance range.] MatrixCare business divestiture (agreement to sell, closing Q1 FY2027, per the same 6 Aug 2026 8-K) removes RMD's slowest-growing segment (Residential Care Software, +5%/+4%cc in FY2026 vs +10%/+8%cc company-wide); size of MatrixCare's standalone revenue/FCF contribution is not disclosed in sources reviewed - data gap.
Insider Form 4 pattern and SBC-as-%-of-revenue not reviewed this pass (data gaps).

RA13 (6 Oct 2026): auditor change - KPMG dismissed 13 Aug 2026, PwC appointed for fiscal 2027 (8-K Item 4.01, acc. 0001193125-26-354154; no disagreements or reportable events); the dossier red-flag scan said no auditor change

RA13: corrected reverse DCF implies 4.3% a year (8.4% cost of equity, SBC-burdened, ex-interest FCFF) rather than 2.4%; $450m accelerated share repurchase executed 31 Aug (8-K acc. 0001193125-26-378487), MatrixCare sold for $490m cash
data_conflicts: b1 quant composite is only mid-quintile (decile 6, quintile 3) despite strong underlying Quality factors (gp/assets, ROE, OCF/assets all top-quartile) because trailing 12-1 month Momentum is weak (pct_mom_12_1 15%) - the composite penalizes a quality name that has underperformed on price, not a fundamental flaw.
RMD.confidence_in_thesis: medium - recurring-revenue quality and balance sheet are primary-sourced; after the cost-of-equity and SBC corrections the valuation cushion is 2.7 points of 10-year growth (0.4 at a 9.4% cost of equity), the auditor changed in August, and the Astral cost and GLP-1 tail are unresolved

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: Corrected 6 Oct 2026 (RA13): the 2.4% implied 10-year growth used WACC 8.0% and FCF of $1,649.5m before stock-based compensation. Rebuilt: FCFF = OCF $1,805.8m - capex $156.3m - patent/intangibles $20.9m - SBC $104.3m - after-tax interest income $39.7m = $1,485m; EV $31.6bn (market cap $32.4bn less net cash $0.81bn); cost of equity 5.17% + 0.77 x 4.14% = 8.4%. Implied 10-year growth 4.3% (6.6% at 9.4%, 8.0% at 10%) against a 10-year base of about 7% (the 9% a year was a 3-year figure). Below, but with a thinner cushion. RMD.scenario_basis: [Corrected 27 Sep 2026: rebuilt without the fabricated FY2027 EPS guidance.] Starting non-GAAP EPS $11.17 (FY2026 actual, confirmed), starting multiple ~19.9x (current TTM non-GAAP P/E - no forward multiple used since no forward guide exists); bear = 2%/yr EPS growth with multiple compressing to 14x (Astral costs escalate, GLP-1 risk shows up, MatrixCare divestiture proceeds disappoint) plus ~1.3% dividend yield; base = 9%/yr EPS growth (delivered organic trend net of MatrixCare drag, offset by buybacks) at a stable ~19.9x multiple plus ~1.2% dividend yield; bull = 13%/yr EPS growth with multiple re-rating to 23x (GLP-1 fear fully dissipates) plus ~1.0% dividend yield.

RTX.thesis_one_line: Aerospace/defense leader with record backlog and repeatedly-raised 2026 guidance, but valuation has already re-rated and the Pratt engine recovery isn't finished.
kill_criteria: Organic sales growth guidance is cut (vs. the current 8-9% FY2026 guide) at any subsequent quarterly update.
PW1100 (GTF) AOG count stops declining or reverses for two consecutive quarters (baseline: down 25% YTD as of Q2 2026).
Net debt/equity rises above 0.60x (currently 0.44x) without a clearly identified, value-accretive acquisition.
FY2026 free cash flow guidance ($8.50-8.75B as of the Q2 2026 release, raised from $8.25-8.75B) is cut. [DVH3 2026-10-06: was stated as $8.25-8.75B as of Q1.]
Adjusted EPS guidance ($7.10-7.25 as of Q2 2026) is cut at the Q3 2026 release (due 20 Oct 2026). [DVH3 2026-10-06: date corrected from ~27 Oct.]
key_adverse_facts: Pratt & Whitney GTF powder-metal contamination/AOG inspection program is not complete; full GTF Advantage production transition is not targeted until 2028.
RTX revenue is government-budget-dependent; continuing-resolution or allied-spending pullback risk is outside company control.

Live legal and compliance matters per the Q2 2026 10-Q: ongoing SEC investigation into the 2023 powder-metal disclosures, securities class action dismissed 12 Sep 2025 and under appeal, two DOJ deferred prosecution agreements plus an SEC administrative order (monitor engaged April 2026, about three years), a State Department consent agreement ($200M penalty, $100M suspended), and DCMA cost-accounting claims (about $1.7B plus $1.6B interest, and $1.1B plus $0.46B interest). RTX does not expect a material adverse effect. [DVH3 2026-10-06; replaces 'not independently re-verified' data-gap line.]

H1 2026 operating cash flow benefited from a $1.5B year-on-year increase from receivables factoring and the 10-Q expects about $0.7B of powder-metal cash outflow in 2026; TTM FCF $11.4B is about 32% above the FY2026 FCF guide midpoint ($8.625B). [DVH3 2026-10-06; replaces the dividend tagging-artefact line: the Q2 XBRL dividend of $1.46 is two real $0.73 declarations.]
data_conflicts: b1 quant composite is only decile 3/quintile 2 (below median) despite strong Momentum (66th pct) and SUE (66th pct), because Value factors are weak (pct_ep 28%) - consistent with a market already paying up for the guidance-raise momentum story.
RTX.confidence_in_thesis: medium - high confidence on backlog/demand and guidance-raise track record; lower confidence on how much of the GTF recovery and demand acceleration is already priced in at the current ~26-27x NTM multiple

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for RTX this wave. NTM P/E on the raised FY2026 guide is ~26-27x, higher than the triage's 24.6x (which predates the Q2 2026 guidance raise) and looks rich in isolation, but this agent's reverse DCF (WACC 8%, 10y explicit + 3% terminal) implies only ~4.2%/year FCF growth is needed versus an 8-9% organic sales growth guide, so the dossier view is fair (not demanding) once FCF conversion and a full decade are modelled rather than just the headline P/E. [DVH3 2026-10-06 restatement: the 8% WACC was not tied to the 5.17% 10-year UST, SBC was not deducted and TTM FCF ($8.36/share) overstates the FY2026 FCF guide ($8.50-8.75B, $6.32/share; $5.44 after stock compensation and 401(k) stock matching of about $1.2B). Programme basis (UST 5.17%, ERP 4.14%, Blume beta 0.52 from raw 0.287, Ke 7.33%, ten years then 3.0% terminal, equity basis): implied 10-year FCF growth is 7.7% on the guide midpoint after SBC (6.7% after stock compensation only; 2.4% on the original TTM basis). The 12%-for-3-years-fading-to-3% base path is worth 1.08x the market price (0.93x at Ke 8.0%): about in line, not below. implied_vs_base below -> in_line; dossier_view fair unchanged; INCLUDE-SMALL unchanged. Scenario returns not changed (re-derived within 0.7 point; the 2% dividend yield is really 1.54%).]

RTX.scenario_basis: Starting adjusted EPS ~$7.175 (FY26 guide midpoint), starting P/E ~24.6x (triage reference); bear = 3%/yr EPS growth with multiple compressing to 18x (GTF issue re-escalates, defense budget squeeze); base = 12%/yr EPS growth at a stable ~24.6x, plus ~2% dividend yield; bull = 18%/yr EPS growth with multiple expanding to 27x (GTF fully resolved, aftermarket boom), plus ~2% dividend yield.

SLB.thesis_one_line: Global oilfield-services leader riding an international upcycle on the revenue line, but GAAP and adjusted profit per share both fell YoY for two straight quarters - confirm the margin pressure is transitory before buying.
kill_criteria: Q4 2026 revenue does not reach the guided >$10B (sequential growth from Q2's $8.97B stalls).
Adjusted EPS YoY growth stays negative for a third consecutive quarter at the Q3 2026 report (due ~16 Oct 2026).
Net debt/EBITDA (TTM EBITDA proxy ~4x Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA) rises above 2.5x.
Buyback pace is cut below the $2.4B full-year-2026 target.
Brent/WTI oil price sustains below $60/bbl for two consecutive quarters.
key_adverse_facts: GAAP net income fell 22% YoY and diluted EPS fell 30% YoY in Q2 2026 despite revenue growth of 5% YoY; adjusted EPS also fell 26% YoY and adjusted EBITDA fell 7% YoY.
Long-term debt (noncurrent) rose from $9,670M to $11,140M in a single quarter (Q1->Q2 2026), a source not independently identified this pass.
Momentum is already extended (+78% over 12 months per the triage's own red flag), and the quant model's bottom-decile composite (driven by value factors) agrees the stock is not statistically cheap.
Sanctions/jurisdictional litigation exposure typical of a large multinational oilfield-services company was not independently re-verified this pass (data gap).
data_conflicts: b1 quant composite is bottom-decile (decile 1, live_rank 448/~500) despite the triage's qualitative quality score of 4/5 - driven by weak Value factors (pct_ep 23%, pct_fcfp 38%, an outlier negative book/price factor) and stretched Momentum (pct_mom_12_1 73%), i.e. the systematic model disagrees with the triage's 'reasonable multiple' read.

The triage's cited '17x NTM multiple' appears to be a forward/hoped-for figure assuming H2 2026 margin recovery; this agent's trailing-four-quarter GAAP P/E is closer to 23x, materially richer, and that recovery has not yet been confirmed by results.
SLB.horizon: not now - reassess at Q3 2026 earnings
SLB.confidence_in_thesis: medium - high confidence on the earnings-quality divergence being real (cross-checked against SLB's own press release); lower confidence on whether it resolves by Q3/Q4 2026 as guided

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for SLB this wave. FCF yield (6.2%) and this agent's reverse DCF (WACC 9%, 10y explicit + 3% terminal, implying only ~2.2%/year FCF growth needed) both suggest the stock is not expensive, consistent with the triage - but that view conflicts with the earnings-quality deterioration (falling GAAP/adjusted EPS) and the quant model's bottom-decile value/momentum read, which is why the verdict is WATCH rather than INCLUDE despite a supportive DCF.

SLB.scenario_basis: Starting adjusted EPS annualized ~$2.20 (Q2 2026 x4), starting P/E ~17x (triage reference); bear = -5%/yr EPS decline with multiple compressing to 11x (oil down-cycle, margin pressure persists), plus ~2.3% dividend yield; base = 8%/yr EPS growth at a stable ~17x (international upcycle plays out as guided), plus ~2.3% dividend yield; bull = 16%/yr EPS growth with multiple expanding to 20x (OPEC+ discipline holds, offshore capex boom), plus ~2.3% dividend yield.
